localChanges: Two findings, both from measuring rather than reading.

**Strings over subclasses, decided by the numbers.** 1,055 rule instances across 163 classes. `replace`/`disable`/`before`/`after` need to name one *instance*, and subclassing cannot — you would need 1,055 subclasses, and the second instance of any class stays unaddressable. Subclasses answer "what kind of rule is this", which the engine already does well. Also records why `before`/`after` reposition instead of computing a priority number, and why every id-taking method throws.
**`01-constraints.md` §4 said Darwin's Voyage was the one unserialisable continuation in the engine. It is one of nine.**

`Unit._busy` is the only field anywhere that holds a `Rule` — 1,055 rules, 4,007 entities, two fields. Five of the thirteen `Busy` subclasses need only an identity and a factory: their criteria are pure functions of the world and the unit, and the durable facts are saved separately.

The other eight come from `DelayedAction.perform`, which closes over `endTurn` and the completion `action`. Neither is recorded, neither is derivable, so a factory would have to invent a completion turn — a unit three turns into a road would load finished or never finishing. They are pending effects in the exact sense 03-save-format.md defines, which makes that mechanism load-bearing rather than a special case for one wonder.
